source.author: verg
source.text: haud segnis strato surgit Palinurus et omnis explorat ventos, atque auribus aera captat; sidera cuncta notat tacito labentia caelo, Arcturum pluviasque Hyadas geminosque Triones, armatumque auro circumspicit Oriona.
source.text_original: haud segnis strato surgit Palinurus et omnis / explorat ventos, atque auribus aera captat; / sidera cuncta notat tacito labentia caelo, / Arcturum pluviasque Hyadas geminosque Triones, / armatumque auro circumspicit Oriona.
source.text_english: Not sluggish, Palinurus rises from his couch and examines all the winds, and catches the air with his ears; he marks all the stars gliding in the silent sky, Arcturus and the rainy Hyades and the twin Triones, and looks about at Orion armed with gold.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quando autem audimus Arcturum et Oriona, non debemus sequi fabulas poetarum, et ridicula ac portentosa mendacia, quibus etiam coelum infamare conantur, et mercedem stupri inter sidera collocare, dicentes: Arcturum, pluviasque Hyadas, geminosque Triones: Armatumque auro circumspicit Oriona:
reuse.text_original: Quando autem audimus Arcturum et Oriona, non debemus sequi fabulas poetarum, et ridicula ac portentosa mendacia, quibus etiam coelum infamare conantur, et mercedem stupri inter sidera collocare, dicentes: Arcturum, pluviasque Hyadas, geminosque Triones: Armatumque auro circumspicit Oriona:
reuse.text_english: When we hear Arcturus and Orion, however, we should not follow the poets’ fables and their ridiculous and monstrous lies, by which they even try to defame heaven and place the wages of debauchery among the stars, saying: Arcturus, and the rainy Hyades, and the twin Triones; and golden-armored Orion looks around him:
